**Sūrat al-Taḥrīm** (The Chapter of Prohibition), also called **Sūrat al-Nabī** (ﷺ) (The Chapter of the Prophet (ﷺ)).

(p-179) Its central purpose is to urge reflection on the proper conduct (*adab*, good manners) owed to Allah, to His Messenger (ﷺ), and to all the servants of Allah, and to encourage adopting legislated good manners (*adab shar'ī*) and fine conduct in dealings, especially with women, following the example of the Prophet (ﷺ) in his good companionship, his noble fellowship, and in showing that proper discipline (*ta'dīb*) sometimes comes through gentleness and patience, at other times through the whip or what is close to it, and at other times through the sword or what is related to it. Both of its names, *al-Taḥrīm* and *al-Nabī* (ﷺ), clarify this.

*Bismillāh al-Ladhī lahu al-kamāl kulluhu 'alā al-dawām* (In the name of Allah, to whom belongs all perfection, forever). *Al-Raḥmān al-Ladhī 'amma 'ibādahu bi-'aẓīm al-in'ām* (the Most Merciful, who has encompassed His servants with great favours). *Al-Raḥīm al-Ladhī atamma khawāṣṣahu ni'mat al-Islām* (the Most Compassionate, who has perfected for His elect the blessing of Islam).

* *

When Allah, glorified is He, concluded the chapter on divorce with the comprehensiveness of His knowledge, and His command descended between the two horizons in His governance, this chapter's opening indicated it by elevating the affairs of creation through a matter that occurred between the best of His creation and his wives, who are among the best of women. Each of them strove to conceal what related to it from him. So Allah, glorified is He, made it manifest as a rebuke to the wives of His Prophet (ﷺ), in the form of a reprimand, because that is more effective in gentleness toward him, since out of his compassion he nearly destroyed his noble self (p-180) out of mercy for his community, sometimes seeking their pleasure and at other times desiring their guidance. For the Prophet (ﷺ) was thorough in refining his character, together with what Allah had purified him with, namely his freedom from every stain, to the extent that he restricted himself by refraining from some of what had been permitted to him, out of consideration for the feelings of others.

Then He, exalted is He, addressed him with the particle of distance, although he is the nearest of those in the divine presence. This is because that particle is suited to matters of great weight and grave, lofty significance, and it contains an allusion to alerting others and making them hear, intending to discipline them, purify them and refine them: **"O Prophet"** (*Yā ayyuhā al-Nabī*). This is an address with the attribute that indicates infallibility, and which most perfectly suits him: serenity of mind, joy of heart and expansion of breast, because he receives from Allah, exalted is He. It urges every listener to keep away from anything that would disturb him (ﷺ) even slightly.

**"Why do you prohibit"** (*Lima tuḥarrim*), meaning, why do you do the act of prohibiting by withholding your noble self from **"what Allah has made lawful"** (*mā aḥalla Allāh*), that is, the King, to whom no one has any command, **"for you"** (*laka*). This refers to the promise, given to some of the Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, to refrain from drinking the honey that was at Ḥafṣa's or Zaynab's, may Allah be pleased with them both, and to refrain from being intimate with your concubine Māriyah, may Allah be pleased with her. Thus you restrict yourself out of excellent companionship with your wives, may Allah be pleased with them all.

The Prophet (ﷺ) used to drink honey at the house of Ḥafṣah bint 'Umar or Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, may Allah be pleased with them both, according to the two differing reports on this in the *Ṣaḥīḥ* (the authentic collection, i.e., of al-Bukhārī and Muslim). In another report: "He (ﷺ) would, when he prayed the morning prayer, enter upon his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, one by one. A jar of honey had been sent as a gift to Ḥafṣah bint 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Whenever he entered upon her and greeted her, she would detain him and give him to drink from it." And 'Ā'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, disliked his lingering with her, so she said to a slave-girl of hers, an Abyssinian woman called Khaṣrah: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enters upon Ḥafṣah, go in to her and look at what he is doing." She reported the matter to her, so she (Ḥafṣah) instructed her female companions, and they made him averse to drinking it by informing him that a foul odour came from him, because a bee had sucked from *al-'Urfuṭ* (a bitter shrub). He said: "I will never return to it." (Reported in the *Ṣaḥīḥ*.)

Al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Mardawayh reported: "He (ﷺ) was alone with Māriyah, may Allah be pleased with her, the mother of his son Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, in the house of Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with her. So Ḥafṣah was aggrieved by that. He said: 'She is forbidden to me. Do not mention this to anyone, and I will give you good news in return for it: Abū Bakr will take charge of this matter after me, and your father after Abū Bakr,' may Allah be pleased with them both. 'Do not inform anyone of this.' But she informed 'Ā'ishah."

It is also reported: "Ḥafṣah, may Allah be pleased with her, said on her day, to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'I have a need to my father, a sum of money he has with him. So permit me to visit him and bring it.' He permitted her. When she went out, he sent for his slave-girl Māriyah the Copt, may Allah be pleased with her, and lay with her. Ḥafṣah came and found the door locked, so she sat down beside it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out, his face dripping with sweat, and Ḥafṣah was weeping. He said to her: 'What makes you weep?' She said: 'You only gave me permission for this! You lay with her on my day and in my bed! Did you not see any respect and right for me? You would not do this with any woman of yours.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Is she not my slave-girl? Allah has made her lawful to me. Be quiet! She is forbidden to me. I seek by that your pleasure. So do not tell anyone of this.' When he went out, she informed 'Ā'ishah, and she made him swear to abandon Māriyah, may Allah be pleased with them all."

Then Allah, glorified is He, gave the reason for this in His saying: **"seeking"** (*tabtaghī*), meaning, you desire with a great desire, out of the noble qualities of your character and the excellence of your companionship, **"the pleasure of your wives"** (*marḍāt azwājika*), that is, the states, situations and matters with which they are pleased. And who is more deserving that you seek your own pleasure? And likewise all creation, so that you may be free for what is revealed to you from your Lord. But this is more emphatic for wives.

And since the highest thing by which the prohibition of things can occur on the part of the servants is faith, and since Allah, exalted is He, had made, out of His mercy to His servants, an expiation (*kaffārah*) for their oaths, He said: **"And Allah"** (*wa-Llāh*), that is, you do that to please them, while the reality is that **"Allah, the King, the Most High, is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful"** (p-183), meaning He erases and veils what is difficult for His sincere servants, and honours them. Then He gave the reason, or explained, in His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 66, verse 2:

﴿Allah has certainly ordained﴾, that is, has decreed, the Possessor of Majesty and Bounty, who has no partner and to whom no one shares authority. He expressed it as "ordained" (*fard*) to encourage accepting the concession (*rukhsah*), indicating that this does not detract from scrupulousness (*wara'*) and does not diminish the sanctity of Allah's name. This is because people of lofty resolve do not like to move from a firm ruling (*'azimah*) to a concession, but rather from a concession to a firm ruling, or from one firm ruling to a similar one.

Since the lightening of the obligation upon this community is only out of His generosity and in honour of this Prophet ﷺ, He said: ﴿for you﴾, that is, O community of which you are the head. He expressed it with a verbal noun that permits what is additional, like His generosity and His honouring, to show the extent of the purpose, and so He said: ﴿the dissolving﴾, that is, the act of dissolving, ﴿of your oaths﴾, that is, something that will release you from what you have bound yourselves to by them, sometimes through the exception (*istithna'*) and sometimes through expiation (*kaffarah*), a great dissolving such that the situation returns to what it was before the oath. This has been explained in Surah al-Ma'idah. So dissolve your oath, and free yourself from your constriction upon yourself, and expand your breast, so that you may receive what comes to you of the tidings of Allah the Exalted while you are free for it with a content soul and a comforted eye.

This indicates that his saying, "You are unlawful to me" (*anti 'alayya haram*), is like an oath if it is not intended as a divorce of the wife or a manumission of a slave woman. And if Allah has ordained this for the whole community to ease matters for them, then their head is more deserving that this be granted to him. Muqatil said: (p-184) So the Prophet ﷺ freed a slave in this incident. It has also been said that his prohibiting (of Mariyah) here was by an oath that he swore, and in that case there is no evidence in it for one who holds that "You are unlawful to me" is an oath. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, while the One singled out with the attributes of perfection, ﴿is your Protector﴾, that is, He will deal with you as a close and sincere friend does. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge of your interests and of other things reaches without end. ﴿The All-Wise﴾, that is, the One who places everything that issues from Him for you in its most perfect place, such that He does not abrogate it, nor can anyone else change it or any part of it.

Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: There is a subtle point in the very close connection of this surah with Surah al-Talaq, because their aim is unified and their meanings are close. He (the Prophet ﷺ) had thought that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had divorced his wives when he withdrew into the upper room, until 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, asked him, and the story is well known. His giving them the choice (*takhyir*) followed from that, and after they had withdrawn from him for a full month. Allah rebuked them in His saying: ﴿And if you two support one another against him, then indeed Allah is his Protector﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], and His saying: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 5]. So this surah and Surah al-Talaq are the closest and most similar of things to Surah al-Anfal and Bara'ah, because of the closeness of their meanings and the interlocking of their purposes. End.

[p. 185] Since the one who sees his beloved distressed, his chest constricted, would first strive to relieve his heart and calm his soul, and then increase his ease by saying to those present: "Our beloved, this noble one among us, such-and-such has happened to him, and I have disliked [this -] and guaranteed its removal," and since Allah, exalted is He, had already comforted his soul ﷺ at the beginning of the surah, then followed it with the other command, the implied sense is: "Remember this that I have mentioned of the good companionship of your Prophet ﷺ toward his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, and his generous fellowship, noble character, [beautiful -] bounties, and great forbearance. And remember what Allah has lightened for you in the oaths that admit no exception (*mathnawiyya*, the principle that an oath may be qualified by a subsequent exception), [and remember in them -] His holy name." Then He joined to this His words, exalted is He, honouring His Prophet ﷺ by addressing him with reproach [upon it -] and by disclosing what bears the weight of this secret, in the most beautiful manner, to lighten his burden and refresh him: ﴿And when﴾, that is, [and -] remember the noble character of the Prophet ﷺ and the pure conduct of his disposition in his dealings with them, when ﴿the Prophet confided﴾, that is, the one whose station Allah always raises by having him receive from the overflowing knowledge of his Lord what he tells people, for ﴿he does not speak from desire﴾. He left the wife unspecified and did not name her, Glory be to Him, as an honour to him ﷺ and to them, may Allah be pleased with them, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿to one of his wives﴾, and she was Hafsa, may Allah be pleased [with her; He concealed -] her, to protect them, because their sanctity, may Allah be pleased with them, is part of his sanctity ﷺ. (p. 186) ﴿a matter﴾, which was not of the concern of the Message. Had it been of the concern of the Message, he would have announced it and not confined it to her, nor kept it secret. This was the prohibition of Mariya, may Allah be pleased with her, his promise to abandon honey, and his giving good news of the leadership of Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them. The matter was not clarified or detailed, out of honour to him ﷺ and to preserve his secret, because it is customary that a person does not wish his secret to be detailed, even though we have come to know of it afterward, so that we may follow his example in what it contains of rulings, for all his states ﷺ are rulings for us, except what was specific to him. He indicated the closeness of the time of its disclosure to the time of the telling by the particle *fa* (then) in His words, exalted is He: ﴿So when she informed﴾, that is, she told [it] with a great and momentous telling, because of its dignity in itself and because it came from Allah, and she exaggerated in that and told ﴿of it﴾ in its entirety, from all its aspects. He placed this in the context of narration because it is more concealing of the sanctity of his household ﷺ, since He did not say: "So she informed [of it -]," nor said: "She wronged by informing of it," or the like of what would be understood as intended in itself. ﴿And Allah made it apparent﴾, that is, the King who has encompassing knowledge of everything made him aware ﴿of it﴾, that is, of the matter, that she had disclosed it, out of sincere counsel to him, by informing him of what occurs in his absence, so that he might warn against it if it is evil and be rewarded for it if it is good. ﴿He made known﴾, that is, the Prophet ﷺ made known to her to whom he had confided ﴿part of it﴾, which was the matter of the caliphate, as a rebuke to her for it, because he had instructed her not to disclose it. Refraining from part of the reproach is more effective in prompting the modesty of the one being rebuked (p. 187) and more helpful toward his repentance and in preventing his returning to the like of it. ﴿And he turned away from part﴾, which was the matter of the secret and the honey, out of generosity on his part, not to press the reproach to its limit, and out of modesty and good companionship. Al-Hasan said: "No noble person ever pressed to the limit." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Overlooking has never ceased to be the conduct of the great." He reproached only regarding the matter of the caliphate, fearing [that it -] might spread among people and be publicized, for it might stir envy from some hypocrites and leave the envious a scheme against the Companion (Abu Bakr) and the Criterion (Umar), or lead to a corruption we do not know of. Al-Kisa'i read it lightened, *'arafa*, meaning he acknowledged it. *Al-ma'rifa* (knowledge) is the cause of *al-ta'rif* (making known), and *al-ta'rif* is from *al-ma'rifa*, so using one for the other is common, and the relation between them is this. He indicated his hastening to make her aware of it, so that what he disliked of her would not spread, by His words: ﴿So when he informed her﴾, of what you did of disclosing what he had made known to her, in a manner that left none of what he had made known to her ﴿of it﴾ nor of its circumstances unmentioned, so that she might become more perceptive. It is reported that she said: "I said to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, in secret, while I knew she would not disclose it." This is what al-Malawi said, and it is the meaning of His words: ﴿She said﴾, that is, supposing that Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, had divulged it to her: ﴿"Who told you this?"﴾, that is, in general terms of information. He began the next words: ﴿He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me."﴾ He omitted the object for brevity of wording and to broaden the meaning by generality, indicating that he informed him of everything that passed between her and Aisha, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and what he had made known to her and what came from others, in its most complete form. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾, that is, the one encompassing in knowledge, ﴿the All-Aware﴾, that is, the one who has knowledge of (p. 188) hearts and outward things. He is worthy to warn, so one should speak neither secretly nor openly except with what pleases Him.

And when he (al-Biqa'i) recognized from this that the one being reproached was two women, and that "the one who informs" (al-Munba'a) comes from the same root as "news" (naba'), and that the number may be given as one while it is in fact two, he pointed out that the two who were reproached were two women. Their hearts had been opened wide to what came to them from God of desirable things [by this reproach concerning this very hidden matter, and by God's generosity to them in it, in not pressing them further. Their hearts therefore inclined toward lofty things, plunged into the sublime knowledges, and fashioned from the jewels of that the subtle meanings. The address turned toward them with gentle kindness] toward the noble return. So He said, as another honouring of him (ﷺ), by turning toward his wives, may God be pleased with them, through the reproach for his sake, standing in for him in what might have disturbed him had he himself confronted it, protecting his noble heart from what might distress him: ﴿If you two repent﴾, that is, O ʿĀʾisha and O Ḥafṣa, for what Ḥafṣa did by divulging (the secret), and what ʿĀʾisha did by devising a stratagem to prevent him from drinking honey and by swearing (an oath) concerning Māriya. ﴿To God﴾, that is, the King whose knowledge encompasses all, whose power is exalted, and who was gentle to them for the sake of him (ﷺ) with the utmost gentleness, in His saying: ﴿for your hearts have inclined﴾, that is, they have leaned and been drawn by what they have fashioned. The plural "hearts" (qulūbukumā) is in the plural of abundance, as an emphasis on what I have understood of the heart's inclination through the abundance of knowledges, by what the revealing of this secret and the reproach for it brought them of shame. Thus they became deserving of hastening to repentance, fully qualified for it.

And when He mentioned what they were truly deserving of by the particle of doubt, to keep the listener between fear and hope in this matter, and He knows best what is to be: the fullest way of doing this is to mention the side of fear. So He said, informing that the King and His allies are helpers for him: ﴿And if you two back each other up﴾ — with the doubled letter (tashdīd) for idgham (assimilation of the two identical consonants) in the reading of the majority (qirāʾa al-jamāʿa), because the consideration here, if it occurred, was in the form of concealment in carrying out the stratagem concerning Māriya, may God be pleased with her, and the honey, and what comes of such things, which jealousy prompts. ﴿Against him﴾, that is, the Prophet (ﷺ), who has been informed by God of what raises his rank and exalts his mention. The reading of the Kufans (qirāʾat al-Kūfiyyīn) is with lightening, by dropping one of the two tāʾs, indicating the ease of this backing-up and the slightness of its harm to him (ﷺ).

And since the meaning is as though He does not care about the backing-up, as He expressed by its cause, He said, emphasizing, to inform that the state of those who back up against him is the state of one who denies the content of the speech: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the Greatest King, for whom there is no equal, ﴿He﴾, that is, in His very Self, the Most Holy, and the presence of the unseen of His unseen, before whose greatness nothing can stand, ﴿is his Protector﴾, that is, his Helper, and the one who takes charge of him, whose affairs are taken in charge by the close, the true, the Capable. Every one who has understanding knows His sufficiency, glory be to Him, in this matter, so He does the most eloquent thing that a protector does with one whose affair he manages. In His helping His Prophet (ﷺ) there is a showing forth of his nobility, a regard for protecting his heart, and an expanding of his breast. [p. 190]

And since souls, for the construction of this abode upon the wisdom of causes, are entrusted with them and look upon them with the most complete look, and since the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), because of the abundance of God's signs and wisdom recited in their houses through the tongue of Jibrīl, peace be upon him, and his frequent coming to the Prophet (ﷺ) in their houses and teaching them, have come to possess through that of the apparent and familiar causes, and since he (Jibrīl) is the greatest of the Prophet's (ﷺ) helpers, He said: ﴿And Jibrīl﴾, because he is among the greatest of the causes which God, glory be to Him, establishes.

And since the one who moves to back him (ﷺ) in [every] what the faith wants, whatever a person is in is more able [to be] the more helpful and supportive, He said: ﴿And the righteous of the believers﴾, that is, those firmly established in the rank of faith and righteousness, from mankind and jinn. Their two parents, may God be pleased with them, are the greatest intended by this. It has been narrated that ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you command me, I will strike off her neck." The word "the righteous" (ṣāliḥ), though its wording is singular, its meaning is the all-encompassing plural, because it is for the genus; and the context indicates this, together with its being annexed to a plural. Perhaps He expressed it in the singular, though this is intended, to indicate the rarity of those who possess this quality [p. 191] greatly, because of the rarity of those firmly rooted in faith and the rarity of those firmly rooted in righteousness among those firmly rooted in faith; so it is a few out of a few. Some have allowed that it is a plural, and that its waw was dropped in the orthography contrary to analogy, and it is dropped in pronunciation due to the meeting of two unvocalized letters; so it is thought to be singular. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, is also included in this.

And since God, glory be to Him and exalted, has given the angels of powers and dominion over the outward and the inward that exceed description, He said, magnifying the station after magnifying it by what He mentioned of the chief of the Cherubim, peace be upon them: ﴿And the angels﴾, that is, all of them, among whom is Jibrīl, peace be upon them, so he is mentioned specifically and generally, three times, to show the intensity of his love and allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ). And since the intended meaning is generality in time and place, after generality among the righteous of angels, mankind and jinn, He said without a preposition, magnifying the support of the angels because of the greatness they have in hearts, since it is established for whoever among mankind has experienced punishment, at one time by the trembling, at another by the thunderbolt, and at another by the sinking of the earth, and at other times by other means. How then when the human, bound by sensible things, imagines their gathering with what they have of the awe-inspiring forms? ﴿After that﴾, that is, after this great matter which has been mentioned, which is the backing-up of God and those mentioned with Him, ﴿is a supporter﴾. He reported of the collective by the name of the genus, [p. 192] indicating that they are of one word in backing-up. Thus He warned with all of this for the sake of the return, showing gentleness to him (ﷺ) and manifesting his greatness. In the story of the companion of Yāsīn, He said: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people﴾ [Yā-Sīn 36:28], the verse, belittling his people and humiliating them. It is also permissible that ﴿supporter﴾ be the predicate of Jibrīl, peace be upon him, and that the predicate of what follows it is omitted, because it is indicated by it, meaning: "likewise."

When he had warned them with what preceded, he increased the warning with something that cuts the hearts, for the hardest thing for a woman is that she be divorced, then that, once divorced, she be replaced, and then that the replacement be better than she. So he said, explaining the least kind of *muẓāharah* (the husband's declaring his wife forbidden to himself), and driving the matter in the manner of hope, as a sign that it suffices the intelligent person, in fear, [the mere possibility -] the likelihood of harm, so how much more when the matter is certain. For it is known that "*ʿasā*" (perhaps, it may be that) from God is in the manner of the great, especially kings, who are content with allusions and symbols. Therefore it is binding, because He is the King of kings, and He alone is truly the Possessor of greatness.

﴿Perhaps his Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to him in all the kinds of goodness you know and those you do not know, is worthy and deserving, and he placed between it and its predicate, out of concern and as a warning, His saying:

﴿if he divorces you﴾, that is, by Himself, without objection to Him, [all of you] or some of you, (p-193) by bringing about divorce for one who has not divorced her and by continuing it for one who has divorced her,

﴿that He replace him﴾ with better than you, by the mere fact of his divorcing you, but without your making him need a search. [It is] a replacement emphasized in the manner indicated by the recitation of Nafiʿ, Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr with *tashdīd* (doubling of the letter), which is more emphatic than the recitation of the rest with *takhfīf* (no doubling), which indicates the general sense of replacement, the suitable and the emphasized and otherwise. And among the honouring [of this matter] is also the attribution of the divorce [to Him] and the replacement to God, together with the expression of the attribute of beneficence, and the specification of the attribution by His pronoun.

Since the most painful thing for a free woman is to be replaced by another free woman and not by a concubine, He said:

﴿wives﴾. And since her being above her in rank is the utmost in grief, He said:

﴿better﴾, and He indicated that it is for preference by His saying:

﴿than you﴾. This is by way of supposition, and it is general in this world and the Hereafter. It does not require the existence of one better than them absolutely, even if it is said that such a one exists in Khadijah, may God be pleased with her, because of what was tested of her restraining herself regarding his right (ﷺ), and her reaching the utmost in his love and in courtesy toward him outwardly and inwardly; and Mary, peace be upon her, who guarded her chastity so that she became among the devout. That is in the Hereafter. The speech comes in the form of a conditional with the divorce, and He, glorified is He, knew that it would not occur. But He, glorified is He, knew that if it did occur, He would replace him (ﷺ) with one who possesses the stated attributes, which require sincerity (p-194) in his obedience, as He indicated by *qānitāt* (devout). And there is no doubt that whoever keeps constant obedience to him and binds her connection to him in both abodes is better than others. The suspension of the divorce of all does not indicate that he did not divorce Hafsah, may God be pleased with her, for it has been narrated that "he divorced her, and that did not increase her except in grace from God, the Exalted, because God, the Exalted, commanded him to take her back, for she was *ṣawwāmah qawwāmah* (much fasting and much standing in prayer)." And God is the Granter of success.

When He had promised what He mentioned, and since the first thing looked at is the outward, He detailed that promise and explained the superiority, beginning with His saying:

﴿Muslims﴾, that is, submitting all their submission, outwardly and inwardly, to God and His Messenger (ﷺ) in the manner of humility.

And since what is seen of Islam is only the outward, He said:

﴿believers﴾, that is, firm in the knowledge-based strength through the affirmation of the inward.

And since that may contain a kind of admixture, He said:

﴿devout﴾, that is, sincere in that, with no admixture in any part of it. So they are at the utmost degree of continuing obedience to him, in humility, submissiveness, and hastening to carry out his command (ﷺ) in ease and in hardship.

And since man is disposed to deficiency, and since sincerity shows its possessor his own shortcoming, and so it may perhaps weaken him, He said, facilitating his service and bringing him closer (p-195) to the continuation of his obedience, teaching courtesy to one in need of it:

﴿penitent﴾, that is, returning quickly from lapses or errors, if anything of that kind happens from them. And since this is what makes worship valid and eases its continuance, He said:

﴿worshippers﴾, that is, continuing in worship by means of the continual renewal of repentance. And since the continuance of worship makes it easy to withdraw from the world, He said:

﴿wanderers﴾, [that is,] characterized by the attributes of the angels, in renouncing the world and absorption in the Hereafter, to the extent that fasting brings about, persevering in that to the utmost of perseverance, so that submission to God and His Messenger (ﷺ) may be complete. For whoever is like this has no desire of his own, and so he is always a follower of his Lord in His command, and becomes gentle in essence and sweet in disposition. Al-Malawi said: "When a woman is much given to fasting and little to eating, her perspiration decreases, her belly shrinks, her scent becomes subtle, and her movement becomes light, for what is desired from her." End of quotation.

The bringing of these attributes in this context is in reproach of one who is characterized by them, making known that the intended meaning is completeness, especially since none of them exists in the manner of firmness without implying the rest. Therefore, in enumerating them, there was no need for the conjunction *wa* (and). Omitting it is more firmly established as indicating that all of them are meant together.

When He had completed the religious attributes that are beneficial in matters of marital companionship, and nothing remained except the natural attributes (p-196), and since the division into one who is acquainted with marriage and one who remains upon the original nature is more delightful and more appealing to the soul, He said, dividing the women who are characterized by the six attributes, joining the second of the two descriptions with *wa* (and) for contrast:

﴿previously married﴾, He put them first because they are more experienced with the companionship whose context this is,

﴿and virgins﴾.

When God had fully admonished the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, while sparing them from being named out of honour for him ﷺ, and knew that they were characterised by these great qualities as a firm and settled trait, arising from their long companionship with him ﷺ, so that they would be among his wives in Paradise, and since their being characterised by that which brought them to the great happiness came only through the good discipline of their guardians over them, and the completion of that discipline through his ﷺ good companionship and their being trained by his noble character, this resulted in the command to the Community to emulate him ﷺ in these perfect qualities, and to emulate their guardians in that, so that they would know the right of God and the rights of their husbands, and thereby reconciliation (ṣalāḥ dhāt al-bayn), which produces all good, would be achieved. So God, the Exalted, following this specific admonition with a general admonition indicating the obligation of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong upon the nearest and then the nearest, said:

﴿O you who﴾, addressing the youngest of the ages, indicating that those above them (p. 197) have already emulated him from the time they entered Islam, so he is independent of a new command, ﴿have believed﴾, meaning, have acknowledged this, ﴿protect yourselves﴾, meaning, make for them a shield by emulating him ﷺ in his manners with creation and with the Creator, and in his gentleness toward whoever deserves gentleness from creation, in glorification of the Creator. So treat him, before anything else, with the same good manners he shows you, and likewise be so with the rest of creation.

Since a person is a shepherd over his household and is answerable for his flock, God, the Exalted, said: ﴿and your families﴾, from among the women, the children, and everyone who falls under this term. Protect them ﴿from a Fire﴾ by counsel and discipline, so that they may be adorned with the character of the People of the Prophet ﷺ, as Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated from Sa'id ibn al-'As, may God be pleased with him, traced back to the Prophet ﷺ: "No father has bestowed upon his child a better gift than good manners." And since things are not magnified in themselves [and -] in the mind of the one informing about them except by informing about what they contain of attributes, He said: ﴿whose fuel is﴾, that is, that with which it is kindled, ﴿men and stones﴾, [that is -] the softest and the hardest of things. Whatever lies between these is, by greater inference, fuel for it.

When He described them with the utmost good manners in obedience, He followed it with a description of the guardians, saying, expressing it with the particle of elevation [indicating their power to exercise authority over it -]: (p. 198) ﴿Over it are angels﴾, [that is, their command over it is by way of elevation -], so it does not disobey them at all, by God's discipline of it. ﴿Stern﴾, that is, [in -] bodies and hearts, harshness toward its inhabitants, because they deserve that by their disobedience to the Supreme King.

Since sternness may exist together with softness, He said: ﴿severe﴾, [that is -] in everything they undertake by word and deed, to the point that it is related that one of them casts seventy thousand unbelievers into the Fire in a single push.

Since the meaning is that they inflict their sternness and severity upon the people of disobedience in proportion to what they deserve, He clarified this with something that shakes hearts, because it is by the command of God, the Exalted, saying: ﴿They do not disobey God﴾, that is, the Supreme King, at any time, ﴿in what He commands them﴾, that is, the command has been issued to them to do it at some time.

Since the one who obeys among us may fall short in some of what is commanded, in its essence, by omitting a pillar, a condition, or a time, through forgetfulness, sleep or the like, or by leaving something recommended or the like, or what is in its meaning through whispering or inner talk or the like, so that he falls short of performing it at the highest degrees, as the Prophet ﷺ said, as recorded by Ibn Majah from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, may God be pleased with them both, and al-Tayalisi from Thawban, may God be pleased with him: "Be upright, and you will not be able to count (your good deeds)," He said, negating this of them: ﴿and they do what they are commanded﴾, that is, renewing themselves with every command on a continuous basis, ﴿whatever they are commanded﴾, that is, whatever command is issued to them at any time, [without any shortfall -] at all, and the verb was put in the passive form without naming its agent, as a metonymy for the ease of their compliance, and as an indication that the one who commands them is known to be God, glorified and exalted be He.

When the Prophet ﷺ was the greatest of those toward whom the community was to be disciplined in good manners (adab) with him, and deliberately violating adab with him amounted to disbelief (kufr), it became clear that this Fire is for those people. So the implied sense is: they will be told, ﴿O you who disbelieved﴾, that is, by violating adab toward the Prophet ﷺ, and that led them to violate adab with God and with the rest of His creation. ﴿Do not make excuses﴾, that is, do not exaggerate in displaying an excuse, which is exerting one's ingenuity to find a plea that would remove the shortcoming that has become evident. ﴿Today﴾, for it is the Day of Recompense, not the Day of Excusing, and the time for excusing has passed, and the matter has come to what it has come to. Since He forbade exaggeration in excusing because it would not benefit them, the prohibition of excusing altogether is a fortiori. This cuts off their hope and imposes silence upon them, so that their concern grows greater and their hearts are cut off, because the meaning is that excusing will not benefit you, even if you exaggerate in it. For this reason He resumed His speech in a restrictive form: ﴿You are only recompensed﴾, that is, on this day, ﴿for what you used to﴾, that is, for what is for you as a natural disposition and innate character, ﴿do﴾ [that is,] in a manner of persistence. There is no improbability for God to form for each person an image of his deed such that he has no doubt that it is his deed, and then to make that image his punishment, in which he finds such pain as He, glorified be He, knows to be commensurate with what he deserves. (p-٢٠٠)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 66, verse 8:

When the command to protect (yourselves and your families from the Fire) and the praise of the angels made clear that those commanded to protect themselves fall short, he said, guiding them to the disease of shortcoming: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. He addressed them with what is most fitting for them, rather than with a particle of distance. ﴿Repent﴾, that is, return with a complete return, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, to the King, for whom there is no equal.

Since every *fa'ūl* in the sense of *fā'il* (an intensive form with active meaning) is used equally for the masculine and the feminine, he said: ﴿a sincere repentance (tawbatan naṣūḥan)﴾. That is, one that is exaggerated in being sincere (nāṣiḥah), by way of a metaphorical attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī, the attribution of a quality to something other than its true bearer), meaning one in which sincerity is given as advice (manṣūḥan fīhā) through purity of intention in three times: in the past, by regret; in the present, by giving up the sin; and in the future, by the resolve not to return to the sin. Thus no relapse occurs in it, just as milk does not return to the udder. And let no one harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for harming his Messenger is harming Him.

Al-Qurṭubī said: the *naṣūḥ* (sincere repentance) comprises four things: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, giving up the sin with the body, resolving in the heart never to return to it, and abandoning evil companions. Ruwaym al-Rā'ī said: it is that you be turned toward Allah with a face and no back, just as you were turned toward disobedience with a back and no face.

When he commanded repentance, he gave as its reason something that yields hope, namely remaining between hope and fear, to make known that this station is the one that saves, because it is the belief in His perfection, and that He, glory be to Him, may do what He wills with the obedient and others. This is by His saying: (p-201) ﴿It may be that your Lord﴾, that is, do this, so that the One who has been good to you by this explanation would be worthy or deserving ﴿to remove﴾, that is, to cover over with a great covering ﴿from you﴾, that is, through repentance, ﴿your misdeeds﴾, that is, whatever of yours has displeased Him. If the penitent is in danger, then what is your opinion of one who persists in his sins?

When he mentioned the benefit of repentance in warding off harms, he mentioned its benefit in bringing about pleasures, and said: ﴿and admit you﴾, that is, on the Day of Decision, ﴿into gardens﴾, that is, orchards with many trees, concealing what is within them, because they are ﴿flowing﴾.

Since that flowing is in part of their land, he expressed it with the particle of partiality: ﴿beneath them﴾, that is, beneath their chambers and trees, ﴿rivers﴾; so they are always watered.

When he mentioned forgiveness and honour, he mentioned its time, saying, giving glad tidings to its people, turning away from others, and praising the people of His affection for His having granted them success and not forsaken them, unlike His enemies: ﴿on the day when Allah will not disgrace﴾, that is, the Supreme King, who has complete encompassing of perfection, ﴿the Prophet﴾, that is, the man whom Allah informs of what necessitates for him the complete elevation, from the reports which are of the greatest magnificence, ﴿and those who believed with him﴾, that is, (p-202) and He will not disgrace those who believed. They are the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, if what is meant is being with him in general time; and those who preceded them, if what is meant is in attribute or in a specific time, such as Badr and the Pledge of Ridwān. For the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one who pledged allegiance under the tree will enter the Fire." This was related by Muslim from Umm Mubashshir, may Allah be pleased with her, and by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī from Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him: "Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent before the victory and fought. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 10], up to His saying ﴿and to each Allah has promised the best﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 10]. And his wives, may Allah be pleased with them, are most worthy of being the first to desire being with him in faith, so that they may be distant from the Fires. If you recall the stories of the prophets from Surah Hūd, upon him be prayers and peace, the goodness of this aspect becomes clear to you. It is also permissible that "those" (alladhīna) be a subject whose predicate is "their light" (nūruhum), or that the predicate be "with him" (ma'ahu), indicating that all the prophets and the righteous of their nations, from his community, are under his banner, and that is at the utmost of nobility and elevation for him (ﷺ). And the faith restricted by being with him means its qualification for companionship with his faith (ﷺ), which is other than unrestricted faith. So there is nothing preventing others among the believers from entering the Fire and then coming out of it by the intercession of the interceders. Therefore the Mu'tazilites (a theological school holding that the grave sinner is eternally in the Fire) have no proof from it that the perpetrator of major sins (al-kabā'ir) abides forever in the Fire, because he who enters the Fire is disgraced, and so he is not described as a believer, since whoever is described as a believer is not disgraced, by the evidence of this verse. Abū Ḥayyān said: (p-203) And in a hadith: "He (ﷺ) pleaded earnestly concerning the matter of his community, and Allah revealed to him: 'If you wish, I will make their reckoning yours.' He said: 'O Lord, You are more merciful to them than I am.' Then He, the Exalted, said: 'Then I will not disgrace you concerning them.'"

When He negated disgrace from them, He explained it by His saying, placing the light first because the context is the magnification of the Prophet (ﷺ), unlike what came earlier in al-Ḥadīd: ﴿their light running﴾, that is, a running that is continually renewed. And according to the other interpretation, this clause is a circumstantial clause. It is also permissible that it be a predicate of "those" if we make it a subject: ﴿before them﴾, and the preposition is omitted to indicate that it fills that direction; "and" likewise "on their right." As for what is on their left, they do not turn to it, because they are either among the foremost or among the people of the right, so they walk between the two directions and receive their records of deeds from them. As for the people of the left, they receive them from behind their backs and from their left, and they, with the light they have, if they speak, they are heard, and if they intercede, their intercession is accepted.

Since perpetuating the dhikr of the King is the most noble attribute of the servant, He said: ﴿they say﴾, that is, renewing this constantly, knowing that Allah, the Exalted, does what He wills, and no one has a right over Him, (p-204) especially when they see the extinguishing of the light of the hypocrites. Sahl said: the need for Allah, the Exalted, does not cease for the believers in this world or in the Hereafter; rather, in the Hereafter they are even more in need of Him, even though they are in the abode of honour, because of their longing for meeting Him: ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who have favoured us with this light and with every good, whether we were or will be in it, ﴿perfect for us﴾. Here they used the imperative because the situation calls for it.

Since a person may be given something and another benefits from it rather than himself, they said: ﴿our light﴾, that is, the one by which You have bestowed Your favour upon us, so that it reaches its utmost completeness, so that You may bring us by it to the place of safety in the abode of peace, and do not make us like the hypocrites whose lights You extinguished, so that their end became darkness.

Since everyone whose manners are good must necessarily regard himself as deficient, they said, in the way of humility, lowliness and submissiveness: ﴿and forgive us﴾, that is, erase from us every deficiency that inclined us toward the states of the hypocrites, both its essence and its effect. This light is the form of their deeds in this world, because in the Hereafter the realities of things become manifest, and forms follow their meanings. It is also the Law of Allah which He legislated, and it is the path (al-ṣirāṭ) that is set up in the midst of Hell. For the virtues in this world are intermediate between the vices, so every virtue is flanked by two vices: excess and deficiency. Virtue is the straight path, and the two vices are what is of Hell on its right and its left. So whoever (p-205) walks in this world according to what he was commanded, without excess or deficiency, his light will be complete. And whoever is inclined by desires, his light is extinguished. May Allah protect us from that and grant us good steadfastness. That extinguishing occurs at some times, and hooks, which are the forms of desires, snatch him, and so he is inclined into the Fire according to the degree of his inclination toward them. And the hypocrite has a light of his confession of the word of tawḥīd, but when he walks it is extinguished, because his confession has no reality; so his light has no reality.

Since what has been mentioned is not able to be done except by Allah, the Exalted, He gave the reason by His saying, emphasizing against the disbelievers' denial of resurrection and what follows from it: ﴿Indeed You﴾, that is, You alone, ﴿over all things﴾, that is, to which the will can enter, ﴿are competent﴾, that is, of perfect power.

(p-206) When he mentioned what preceded of his gentleness ﷺ toward the weakest of people, women, his good manners, and his noble companionship, because he is inclined to compassion for God's servants and mercy toward them, and when He concluded with what honor belongs to the believers and with the completeness of God's power, that produced the decisive matter of humbling and disgracing their enemies. So He said, addressing them with consideration for the gravity of that day, while [the Prophet is] the most sincere of creation [so that he may be] ﷺ, combining in his obedience to Him, glorified and exalted is He, the opposites of gentleness and severity, contentment and anger, forbearance and retribution, and others. This is more indicative of worshipping God by what He commanded, glorified and exalted is He, and of adorning oneself with His commands and with everything that pleases Him: ﴿O Prophet﴾, addressing him with the particle of mediation (tawassut, the particle indicating the middle position), to make the Ummah al-Wusta (the Middle Community, the community of the middle path) hear, as an alert that they are in reality the ones being addressed. Because of its indication of mediation, and God knows best, it is never followed except by what has great importance, expressing himself with the descriptive form that indicates elevation, by informing of divine reports, which is based on firmness and greatness, and which produces dominance. As for the description of the Message, mercy predominates in it, so his turning toward gentleness and kind management increases, in view of the description of Lordship: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers﴾, that is, those who openly display everything that exhausts them, restraining them from the sword and what is less than it, so that he knows that the lions acquired [their courage] only from your might. Thus he knows that this gentleness toward the people of God is only from the completeness of your intellect, the abundance of your knowledge and virtue, your great forbearance, your fear of God, and your nobility. ﴿And the hypocrites﴾, that is, those who conceal [their disbelief] with what befits them of argument if they persist in concealment, and with the sword if it is needed, should they show any kind of support [for the disbelievers]. ﴿And be harsh﴾, that is, be harsh in deed and word, with rebuke, reproach, distancing, and abandonment ﴿toward them﴾, for harshness toward them is part of gentleness toward God, just as gentleness toward the people of God comes from the fear of God. He, glorified is He, had commanded him to be gentle [toward them] at the beginning of the matter, to remove their excuses and to make clear their persistence. When he reached the furthest extent of gentleness, he passed beyond it to harshness and surpassed it. This verse makes clear that the comparative form in the saying of the women to ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him: "(p-207) You are harsher and rougher than the Messenger of God ﷺ," is used in its proper sense, and there is no objection to it.

Since the retribution of the friend against the enemy is only for God, glorified and exalted is He, and he has no share in it, it necessitates that God does not rely on him concerning the friend's right. So the implied meaning is: they have no protection or sanctity in this world, nor any strength, even if the matter of them appears otherwise. He joined to it His saying: ﴿And their refuge﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿is Hell﴾, that is, the fiery abode in which one meets, within it, scowling and loathing.

Since the implied meaning is: their destination is inevitably to it, He joined to it His saying: ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, that is, it is so. That is God's recompense for them for their wrongdoing against His friends and their belittling of His beloved ones.

When the uprooting [of the wicked] in both salvation and destruction was most like the state of the people of the Hereafter in the judgement, with justice and grace, and since the surah had opened with a rebuke of the women, then followed with the command to discipline the entire community, concluding with the destruction of the one who opposes [the Prophet] in both abodes, and since the disbelievers had kinship ties with the Muslims and thought these might benefit them, and the Muslims had kinship ties with the disbelievers and might have imagined these would harm them, He said, answering what might be imagined from that, as a discipline for whoever among the women and others would object to him (ﷺ): ﴿Allah has struck an example﴾. [That is, the King] who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿an example﴾ by which those who have the capacity for knowledge know, and by which those who have the capacity to be admonished are admonished. ﴿For those who disbelieved﴾, meaning those who concealed the truth from themselves and from others, whether they were opponents or hypocrites, in that they do not benefit, despite their disbelief, from the connection and ties that exist between them and the believers. So they will be treated harshly in both abodes, with dealing commensurate with what they deserve, without favouritism toward anyone, however exalted his station, high his rank, or lofty his aim, because disbelief severs the ties between the disbeliever and the Muslim. ﴿The wife of Noah﴾, whom Allah destroyed by drowning for her lying, while he, upon him be peace, was helped and sheltered; her name, it is said, was Wāʿila. ﴿And the wife of Lot﴾, whom Allah also destroyed for her lying, by the stones, the sinking and the drowning; her name, it is said, was Wāhila. He indicated the aspect of the comparison by His saying ﴿they were﴾, meaning, despite both being disbelievers. He did not say "under them," but rather by the attribute of servitude, which is attributed to Him, glorified and exalted, and by the attribute of righteousness, because that is more majestic, so it would be more effective and greater in its impact on the one being admonished, and to prevent anyone from imagining something unfitting to their station, upon them be peace. So He said: ﴿under two of Our servants﴾, meaning each of them was under a servant. He expressed it this way because the people's standing before the King, as was mentioned earlier, is that they are His servants, and He indicated the multitude of His servants as an alert to His self-sufficiency, by His saying: ﴿from Our servants﴾.

Since the degrees of nearness vary according to righteousness, He said: ﴿righteous﴾, and they are Noah and Lot, upon them be peace. ﴿But they betrayed them﴾ by not following them in religion, a hypocrisy on their part, not by betrayal in the marital bed, for Allah has preserved all the prophets from that. None of them said, on account of their disbelief: "My Lord, make me with Your Prophet in Paradise." He also indicated that intercession is not accepted for one who has wronged the Beloved, and that he will certainly be punished, for the satisfaction of the avenger, by His saying: ﴿so they did not avail them﴾, meaning, as a consequence, the two righteous servants did not avail them, meaning the two women, by the right of marriage, ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning against the punishment of the King to whom the command belongs entirely, so there is no command for anyone else, ﴿in anything﴾, meaning of any benefit, because of their betrayal through opposition in religion. He indicated the perfection of His power, exalted is He, by the use of the passive form, so He said: ﴿And it was said﴾, meaning to the two women, by one who was permitted to speak the binding word that cannot be turned back: ﴿Enter the Fire﴾, meaning its preliminaries, from persistence in disbelief, then destruction by the punishment of vengeance in this world, and its reality in the Hereafter, because Allah hated them, for they were enemies to His friends. This is as it is said: "The enemy of my friend is not my friend."

When the two women did the deeds of men in their independence and in not regarding themselves as followers, their punishment was made severer by being with the men in their punishment. So He said, indicating the enforcement of the judgement upon one stronger than them after its enforcement upon them: ﴿with those who enter﴾, meaning those who are greater than them, among those who have a connection with the people of Allah and those who have no connection with them. So let every person conduct himself toward the Prophet (ﷺ) with the utmost courtesy, out of fear of the like of that. This removes the hearts from anyone who began to discipline them, may Allah be pleased with them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 66, verse 11:

When he had completed the like of the warning, that the obedience of the obedient does not benefit the disobedient, even if he is the nearest of people to the obedient, unless there is a foundation upon which the building can stand, and which it is permissible to rely upon and to consider, he followed it with the like of the good news, that the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm the obedient. So he said: ﴿And Allah sets forth an example for those who believe﴾, that is, the Sovereign, the Most High, who possesses the attributes of perfection, [sets forth an example] for those who believe, even if they are at the lowest degrees of faith, clarifying that association with disbelievers, when it is under compulsion and coercion, does not harm: ﴿the wife of Pharaoh﴾, whose name was Asiyah daughter of Muzahim. She believed and did righteous deeds, so her association with the disbeliever through marriage, which is among the greatest of bonds, did not harm her, and her faith did not benefit him. ﴿Every person is a pledge for what he has earned﴾ [al-Tur: 21]. Her Lord, glorified is He, rewarded her by making her the wife of the best of His creation, Muhammad (ﷺ), in the abode of His honour, for her patience in worshipping Allah while she was under the authority of His enemy. He dropped the description of her as His servant, as a sign of his contempt and of the lack of mercy towards him, for he was the greatest of His enemies. He indicated the aspect of resemblance in the example, (p-211) which is her withdrawal to the party of Allah to the extent of her ability, [so] he said: ﴿When﴾, that is, their likeness is her likeness, when ﴿she said﴾, confirming with belief, calling out with the call of the elect, omitting the particle for the sake of her being a believer, even though she was under a disbeliever who was with us, so his companionship did not harm her in any way because of her faith: ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O You who have shown kindness to me by guidance, while I am under the authority of this disbelieving tyrant, and the glitter of worldly might and its abundance did not deceive me: ﴿Build for me﴾.

Since the neighbour is sought, as they say, before the house, she asked for the best of neighbours, and she placed the adverbial phrase first, out of concern for it, because it explicitly states the nearness and indicates closeness to Him. So she said: ﴿a house with You﴾, and she specified her intended meaning by "with You" and said: ﴿in the Garden﴾, because it is the abode of those brought near. Thus it became clear from the beginning and end of her speech that what she sought was the most special of His abodes. He, glorified is He, answered her by making her the wife of the seal of His messengers, who is the best of His creation and the nearest of them to Him, so she was with him in his dwelling, which is the highest of dwellings.

When she asked for what would bring her close to the presence of Allah, she asked for what would keep her far, in both abodes, from His enemies. So she said: ﴿And save me﴾, that is, a great salvation, ﴿from Pharaoh﴾, that is, so that I am not with him, and do not let him have power over me in a way that harms me in Your sight, ﴿and his deeds﴾, that is, that I should act in any way like him. ﴿And save me﴾: she repeated the verb for emphasis, ﴿from the wrongdoing people﴾, that is, the strong people who are firmly set in placing their deeds in other than the places where they were commanded to place them, the conduct of one who walks in darkness generally, and they are the Copts. Do not let me mix with any of them. So Allah, the Exalted, answered her supplication and was gracious to her, for the sake of her love for the Beloved, who is Moses, peace be upon him, as it is said: "The friend of my friend is included in my friendship." That was because when Moses, peace be upon him, overcame the magicians, she believed in him, so Pharaoh tortured her, and she died after Allah showed her her house in the Garden. Her being under Pharaoh did not harm her in any way, because she was excused in that. So the verse is of the type of ihtibak: the first part omits "so she did not ask for the Garden," which is indicated by the second "Build for me," and the second part omits "she was under a disbeliever," which is indicated by the first.

The first part of the passage is the second half of a comparison that al-Biqa'i draws between two groups of women: those whose association with the righteous did not benefit them, and those whose good conduct brought them benefit. He introduced the comparison in the previous verse and now turns to the example of Maryam.

Al-Biqa'i presents the Prophet's words, related by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him: "Many men have attained perfection, but among women only Maryam, daughter of 'Imran, and Asiya, wife of Pharaoh, have attained perfection. And the superiority of 'A'isha over women is like the superiority of tharid (bread soaked in broth) over other food." Along with her equality with them in perfection, the two situations differ in being previously married and in being a virgin, a contrast. Allah did not test the Prophet's wife (ﷺ) by mixing her with ... [بِخَلْطِهِ زَوْجَ] ... (the bracketed reading of the edition), combining the categories of previously married women and virgins that Allah bestowed on His Prophet (ﷺ). She conducted herself well toward herself and toward Allah and toward all of His servants with whom she was bound to observe proper conduct. Allah dealt well with her, granting her care in return for the goodness He had enabled her to do (p-213), and this care was for her forebears, since they were among the greatest beloved servants.

Allah said: ﴿And Maryam﴾, meaning: Allah set forth an example for those who were solitary and withdrawn among those who believed: Maryam ﴿daughter of 'Imran﴾, meaning one of the beloved servants. He mentioned the point of resemblance, saying: ﴿who guarded her chastity﴾, meaning she abstained from evil and from all its preliminaries, with a chastity that was like a great fortress preventing an enemy. She persisted in her virginity until death, so He married her in Paradise as a reward for her, to the best of Our servants, Muhammad (ﷺ), seal of the prophets and imam of the messengers.

When she was content in her companionship with the Spirit of Allah, which He had breathed into her heart through love of remembrance and worship, rather than in companionship with human spirits, this was the cause of His bestowing upon her a Spirit from Him, which He embodied in the most perfect form that was decreed for that time. He spoke, telling of this, saying: ﴿So We breathed﴾, meaning by Our greatness, through Our angel as intermediary, the Holy Spirit.

Since this surah is for honouring the Prophet (ﷺ) and perfecting his wives in this world and the Hereafter, He stated the intended matter explicitly by using the masculine pronoun and did not feminize it, to close the mouth of one who says, out of obstinacy, that what is meant is the breathing of her spirit into her body. ﴿into it﴾, meaning into her true opening, which is the front of her garment, and every opening of a garment is called a farj (opening). The first meaning is indicated by the irregular (shadhdh) recitation fiha (into her), which is a non-standard qira'a (recitation). ﴿from Our Spirit﴾, meaning a spirit that is worthy of its nobility, by what We have magnified of Our creation and the subtlety of its formation, that it should be attributed to Us, because it is outside the usual causal chain. It is Jibril, peace be upon him, or the Spirit of life.

Since the sense is: "So what We willed came to pass," she conceived without any man touching her, and she bore 'Isa, peace be upon him, who was from Our word, which was "Be!" Then Our word "Be, O womb, without a man" and then Our word "with him, O Maryam, without a helper" and then Our word "'Isa will speak in the cradle with wisdom." He joined to this His saying: ﴿and she confirmed﴾, so she deserved for this to be called siddiqa (one who affirms the truth). ﴿the words of her Lord﴾, meaning the One who had bestowed good upon her by what has preceded and other things, of the words spoken by Jibril, peace be upon him, on account of it, and from 'Isa, peace be upon him, and what he said about Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. ﴿and His books﴾, meaning and His Book that gathers and governs His speech, which He sent down to her son and to others among the books of Allah, as the recitation of the people of Basra and Hafs, with the plural form, indicates.

Since the one who confirms may confirm only outwardly, or with some mixture of inner motives, He said: ﴿and she was﴾, meaning by natural disposition and inclination, and He honoured her by placing her in the rank of the most perfect, who are men, so He said: ﴿of the devoutly obedient (qanitin)﴾, meaning the sincere ones who are at the utmost strength and perfection, because she was among the daughters of the beloved, chosen above all peoples. Her worship did not fall short of the worship of the strong in word. Allah, the Glorified, has perfected the examples concerning conduct through the previously married women and virgins, the righteous and the wicked, so the end of the surah corresponds in meaning to its beginning regarding conduct. This is increased in goodness by the fact that she is among women, in persons and individuals, through the marriage of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Asiya, wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam daughter of 'Imran, in Paradise, the abode of permanence, safe from troubles, [the everlasting marriage -] (variant reading). Thus the beginning and end of the surah are about his wives (ﷺ), and its closing with devout obedience (qunut), which is the essence of the qualities mentioned earlier concerning the substitutes mentioned, is the most fitting correspondence. And Allah is the Guide.
